61/S0.subgoal: Introduce the Unity developer environment as a platform for implementing virtual and augmented reality systems.

61/S1.subgoal: Describe the various render pipelines (Built-in, URP, HDRP, and custom) supported by Unity.

61/S2.subgoal: Explain how Unity uses models, meshes, materials, and textures to define 3D objects.

61/S3.subgoal: Describe the tools Unity provides for creating and manipulating environmental scenes, including terrain and skyboxes.

61/S4.subgoal: Explain how Unity handles realistic lighting calculations and the application of visual effects.

61/S5.subgoal: Describe how the camera concept in Unity manages the view transformation and rendering pipeline.

61/S6.subgoal: Explain the role and types of native graphics libraries that Unity supports for implementation.

61/S7.subgoal: Introduce the concept of physics simulation and the core components used in Unity.

61/S8.subgoal: Define and explain the function of rigid bodies and colliders in physical simulations.

61/S9.subgoal: Explain how joints and articulation function to model realistic object movement.

61/S10.subgoal: Describe how the articulation body class facilitates complex, realistic character movements in Unity.

61/S11.subgoal: Explain Unity's sophisticated animation system and workflow for character movements.

61/S12.subgoal: Describe how Unity implements audio support using components like the Audio Source, Listener, and Filters.

61/S13.subgoal: Summarize the advanced graphics and audio features covered in the lecture.
